description: Answerable's staff-only admin MCP: organisations, users and members (including stopping someone), groups, access, single sign-on, the audit log, the Toolbox and standalone MCPs in Answerable ID, each tool behind a staff role.

tools.name: access_enable
tools.description: Prepare enabling a disabled entitlement of an organisation in Answerable ID, so that it grants its scopes again: the inverse of access_revoke. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. Find the entitlement with access_list, status disabled.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: access_grant
tools.description: Prepare granting scopes on a resource, such as the Toolbox's grant strings, to a whole organisation, one of its groups or one member in Answerable ID, optionally through one OAuth client only; a standalone MCP's resource needs the client, claude-code-<name>. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. Every scope must be one the resource allows. ID keeps one entitlement per principal and target.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

kind.description: organization: everyone in it; group: one group's members; member: one person

id.description: The group's or the member's id; omit it for organization

resource.description: The resource it reaches, as registered in Answerable ID, such as the Toolbox's MCP URL

clientId.description: Only through this OAuth client; omit it for every client, except on a standalone MCP's resource, where it is required: claude-code-<name>

scopes.description: The scopes or grant strings to grant, each allowed by the resource

tools.name: access_list
tools.description: List the entitlements of an organisation, newest first, 20 per page by default and at most 100. Each names who holds it (memberId, else groupId, else the whole organisation), the client and resource it reaches, its scopes, status and validity window. A row with a clientId reaches its resource through that client only: toolbox_enable makes one per host client, carrying toolbox, beside the grants for people. Filter by clientId, resource, memberId, groupId and status. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor. Changes nothing.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

clientId.description: Only entitlements for this OAuth client

resource.description: Only entitlements for this resource URL

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit it for the first page

tools.name: access_revoke
tools.description: Prepare disabling an entitlement of an organisation in Answerable ID, so that it grants nothing; access_enable enables it again. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. Deleting an entitlement is not possible through the admin MCP. Find the entitlement with access_list.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: admin_whoami
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Read who you are to the Answerable admin MCP: your user, membership, organisation and host client, your staff role as Answerable ID says it on this call (team, admin or owner; null, with how to get one, when you hold none) and the tools that role lets you use. Call it first, and when a tool you expect is missing. Changes nothing.

organizationId.description: The platform organisation

clientId.description: The OAuth client of the host you are using

role.description: team reads; admin also makes ordinary changes; owner also runs the critical operations; null: none

nextStep.description: How to get a role, when you hold none

tools.description: The tools you may call, by the names hosts list

tools.name: audit_list
tools.description: List Answerable ID's audit events, newest first, 20 per page by default and at most 100, across every organisation or one. requestId is the x-request-id of the call that caused the event: for a change made through the admin MCP, the execution id in its evidence. operationId is ID's operation; filter by it to follow one change. from is inclusive, to exclusive. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor. Changes nothing.

organizationId.description: Only events of this organisation; omit for every organisation

action.description: Exactly this action, such as organization.created

actorId.description: Only events by this user id or client id

operationId.description: Only the events of this ID operation

targetType.description: Only events on this kind of target, such as organization

from.description: From this time, inclusive, in UTC

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit it for the first page

requestId.description: The x-request-id of the call that caused it

operationId.description: ID's operation, null for an event outside one

tools.name: admin_commit
tools.description: Commit an agent-class intent that a prepare tool returned: pass its intent_id and commit_token. Returns the receipt; calling again returns the same receipt with idempotent_replay true. An intent whose commit_tool is admin_commit_confirmed answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED here.

intent_id.description: intent_id from the prepare tool's result

commit_token.description: commit_token from the prepare tool's result; it works once

tools.name: admin_commit_confirmed
tools.description: Commit a controlled-class intent once the person has seen its preview and confirmed it: pass its intent_id, commit_token and preview_summary, which must equal the intent's preview.summary word for word. Returns the receipt; calling again returns the same receipt with idempotent_replay true. A human-class intent needs a person's approval and answers APPROVAL_REQUIRED; commit an agent-class intent with admin_commit.

intent_id.description: intent_id from the prepare tool's result

commit_token.description: commit_token from the prepare tool's result; it works once

preview_summary.description: The intent's preview.summary, word for word as the person saw it

tools.name: domains_add
tools.description: Prepare routing an email domain to an organisation in Answerable ID, so that people with that domain are sent to its sign-in: a magic link, its directory, or the choice of both. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. A domain belongs to one organisation, and a public mail domain is refused. The result gives the DNS record that proves it, which domains_verify checks; sso_set connects a directory, if it has one.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

domain.description: The email domain, such as newco.example

verificationRecord.description: The TXT record that proves the domain; null when ID replayed the write, and organisations_get shows it

tools.name: domains_verify
tools.description: Prepare checking an organisation's email domain in DNS with Answerable ID: a TXT record at _answerable-challenge.<domain> with the value domains_add and organisations_get give. Found, the domain is proved. Not found on a domain already proved, the proof is cleared, so that it fails closed. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. magiclink_admission needs every active domain proved before anyone at them may ask for a link.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

domain.description: The email domain, as organisations_get shows it

verifiedAt.description: When the record was seen; null when ID replayed the write, and organisations_get shows it

tools.name: groups_addmember
tools.description: Prepare putting a member in a group of their organisation in Answerable ID, optionally until a time, or changing when their membership ends. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. The member gains what the group's entitlements grant. A person is a member once they have signed in.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

validUntil.description: When the membership ends, ISO 8601; omit for no end

tools.name: groups_create
tools.description: Prepare creating a group in an organisation in Answerable ID, with a slug unique in the organisation and a name. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. Add members with groups_addmember and give the group access with access_grant.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

slug.description: Unique in the organisation, such as engineers

tools.name: groups_dropmember
tools.description: Prepare taking a member out of a group of their organisation in Answerable ID. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. The member loses what the group's entitlements granted them, unless something else grants it.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: groups_list
tools.description: List the groups of an organisation, newest first, 20 per page by default and at most 100: id, slug, name and status. Filter by q, text in the name or slug, and by status. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor. Changes nothing; members_get shows the groups of one member.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

q.description: Text to find in the name or slug

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit it for the first page

tools.name: magiclink_admission
tools.description: Prepare setting who may ask an organisation for a magic link in Answerable ID. listed: its effective members. domain: also anyone with an address at a domain that has passed domains_verify, whom a first sign-in creates; that needs the owner role, and every active domain proved. Removed members and disabled people are refused in both. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. It ends no session and no grant, and existing members stay members.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

admission.description: listed: the organisation's effective members; domain: also anyone at one of its proved domains

tools.name: magiclink_disable
tools.description: Prepare turning sign-in by emailed link off for an organisation in Answerable ID: its magic-link sessions and grants end, and directory sign-ins, sessions and grants are not touched. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. This is how an organisation requires its directory only. magiclink_enable reverses the setting, not what it ended.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: magiclink_enable
tools.description: Prepare turning sign-in by emailed link on for an organisation in Answerable ID, whether or not it has a directory. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. magiclink_admission says who may ask for a link; the platform organisation can never use them.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: members_get
tools.description: Read one member of an organisation: their user, email, name, status and validity window, the groups they belong to, and their access: each client and resource their entitlements reach, with the scopes and the entitlements (organisation-wide, a group's or their own) that grant them. memberId is the id from members_list. Changes nothing.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

id.description: The member id: the person's membership of this organisation

effective.description: Whether the membership is in force now

id.description: The client id, or for kind resource the resource

via.description: The entitlements that grant it: organisation-wide, a group's or the member's own

access.description: What the member's entitlements reach, from ID's member access view

tools.name: members_import
tools.description: Prepare listing people in an organisation in Answerable ID before their first sign-in, so that their sub exists first: a user and an active membership for each address, at most 1,000, and no account, which the first sign-in makes. Each address has its own answer, and one refused does not stop the rest: refused when invalid, outside the organisation's active domains, public mail, a disabled person, a removed member, whom only members_reinstate brings back, or an account of another organisation. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. It sends no mail, and works with magic links off and with a directory connected.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

items.description: An email address, in any case

addresses.description: The addresses to list, at most 1,000; repeats count once

counts.description: How many had each outcome; null when ID replayed the write, and audit_list by operationId shows who it made

refused.description: The refused addresses and why, the first 20

tools.name: members_list
tools.description: List the members of an organisation, newest first, 20 per page by default and at most 100: member id, user id, email, name, status and whether the membership is in force now. A person becomes a member at their first sign-in, or when members_import lists them. Filter by exact email, by q, text in the email or name, and by effective. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor. Changes nothing.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

q.description: Text to find in the email or name

effective.description: Only members whose membership is, or is not, in force now

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit it for the first page

id.description: The member id: the person's membership of this organisation

effective.description: Whether the membership is in force now

tools.name: members_reinstate
tools.description: Prepare reinstating a person removed from one organisation in Answerable ID, so that they can sign in to it again. Name the member by memberId or email. A person who is Answerable staff needs the owner role. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. The direct grants and group assignments removed with the membership are not restored.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

memberId.description: The member's id, from members_list; give this or the email, not both

email.description: Their address as Answerable ID holds it, in any case; give this or the id, not both

tools.name: members_remove
tools.description: Prepare removing a person from one organisation in Answerable ID: their membership there is revoked, their direct grants and group assignments in it are removed, and they cannot sign in to it. Their other organisations stay as they are. Name the member by memberId or email. A person who is Answerable staff needs the owner role. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. members_reinstate brings the membership back, not the grants and assignments; users_disable stops them everywhere.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

memberId.description: The member's id, from members_list; give this or the email, not both

email.description: Their address as Answerable ID holds it, in any case; give this or the id, not both

tools.name: organisations_create
tools.description: Prepare creating an organisation in Answerable ID with a unique slug and a name. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. It starts with no domain, directory, member or access, and with magic links on for its members: then domains_add, members_import or sso_set, toolbox_enable and access_grant. A directory is one way in, not the only one.

slug.description: Unique in Answerable ID: lowercase letters and digits, words joined by single hyphens, such as newco

tools.name: organisations_disable
tools.description: Prepare disabling an organisation in Answerable ID: its people can no longer get tokens, and every grant it has is revoked. Owner only, with a recent sign-in at your directory. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. organisations_enable reverses the status, not the revoked grants.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: organisations_enable
tools.description: Prepare enabling a disabled organisation in Answerable ID, so that its people can sign in again. Owner only, with a recent sign-in at your directory. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. Grants revoked when it was disabled stay revoked: people sign in again.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: organisations_get
tools.description: Read one organisation from Answerable ID: its slug, name and status, and its two ways in side by side, each with its own state. magicLink: whether links are on, who may ask for one and how many effective members it lists. sso: its directory, issuer, domain, whether it signs in through Answerable's platform application or its own credentials and whether a client secret is set, null when it has none. Also every email domain routed to it, each with when it was proved and the DNS record that proves it. Changes nothing.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

verifiedAt.description: When its DNS record was last seen; null until domains_verify finds it

verificationRecord.description: What the organisation publishes in DNS to prove the domain

domains.description: Every email domain routed to the organisation

admission.description: Who may ask for a link: listed, its effective members; domain, also anyone at a proved domain

magicLink.description: Sign-in by emailed link; independent of the directory

credentials.description: platform: Answerable's Google or Microsoft application; own: the organisation's

tools.name: organisations_list
tools.description: List the organisations in Answerable ID, newest first, 20 per page by default and at most 100: id, slug, name and status. Filter by q, text in the name or slug, and by status. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor for the next page. Changes nothing; organisations_get reads one organisation's domains and SSO provider.

q.description: Text to find in the name or slug, in any case

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit it for the first page

tools.name: organisations_update
tools.description: Prepare renaming an organisation in Answerable ID; the slug never changes. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. The commit sends the organisation's version as If-Match, so a change made meanwhile is refused.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

tools.name: sso_set
tools.description: Prepare setting or replacing an organisation's SSO provider in Answerable ID, through Answerable's own Microsoft or Google application: a Microsoft Entra issuer https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant id>/v2.0 or https://accounts.google.com. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. A directory with its own credentials needs a client secret, which no tool takes. Directory sessions and grants end when it changes; magic links, their sessions and their grants stay as they are.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

issuer.description: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant id>/v2.0 for Microsoft Entra, or https://accounts.google.com

domain.description: The email domain people sign in with, such as newco.example

tools.name: sso_test
tools.description: Run Answerable ID's connectivity test of an organisation's SSO provider: whether its discovery document and signing keys can be fetched and whether the issuer matches, with each problem found. ID refuses an issuer over plain HTTP, such as a local test directory. Changes nothing; organisations_get shows which provider is set.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

keys.description: How many signing keys it publishes

tools.name: staff_grant
tools.description: Prepare giving a member of the Answerable platform organisation a staff role on this admin MCP, by adding them to a group whose entitlement carries the role. Owner only, with a recent sign-in at your directory. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. It applies to their next request.

memberId.description: The member's id in the platform organisation, from staff_list

role.description: team reads; admin also makes ordinary changes; owner also runs the critical operations

tools.name: staff_list
tools.description: List the members of the Answerable platform organisation who can reach this admin MCP, newest first, 20 per page by default and at most 100, each with their staff role (team, admin or owner, or null when they hold none), read from Answerable ID whatever their groups are called. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as cursor. Changes nothing.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit it for the first page

tools.name: staff_revoke
tools.description: Prepare taking a staff role on this admin MCP away from a member of the Answerable platform organisation, by removing them from every group whose entitlement carries the role. Owner only, with a recent sign-in at your directory. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. It applies to their next request.

memberId.description: The member's id in the platform organisation, from staff_list

role.description: team reads; admin also makes ordinary changes; owner also runs the critical operations

tools.name: standalone_enable
tools.description: Prepare giving an organisation access to a standalone MCP, which the Toolbox serves at its own URL: for its host client, claude-code-<name>, its link to the MCP, the organisation's sign-in and MCP capabilities for both grant kinds, and the sign-in entitlement for everyone in it. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. People then need the MCP's scopes through that host client: access_grant them with clientId set to it, to the organisation, a group or a person, or pass everyone: true to grant them to the whole organisation in the same intent. Undo it with access_revoke. Safe to repeat.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

mcp.description: The standalone MCP's name, as bun mcp list shows it, such as acme

everyone.description: Also grant the MCP's scopes to everyone in the organisation, through its host client; omit it to grant them with access_grant

created.description: What the commit made in Answerable ID

existing.description: What it found already in place

tools.name: toolbox_enable
tools.description: Prepare enabling the Toolbox for an organisation: the named providers in its catalogue, and for each named host client what Answerable ID needs so that its people can sign in to the Toolbox from it. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. What each person may use still needs access_grant of grant strings. Safe to repeat.

organizationId.description: The organisation's id in Answerable ID, from organisations_list

hostClientIds.description: The OAuth clients people use the Toolbox from, such as claude-code-toolbox

providers.description: The Toolbox providers to enable, such as e2e; the Toolbox lists them

existing.description: What it found already in place

tools.name: users_disable
tools.description: Prepare disabling a person in Answerable ID at every organisation they belong to, not one: their sessions, grants and stored tokens end, and no sign-in works for them. Name them by email or userId. A person who is Answerable staff needs the owner role. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. users_enable reverses the status, not what was revoked; members_remove stops them at one organisation only.

email.description: Their address as Answerable ID holds it, in any case; give this or the id, not both

userId.description: Their user id, from members_list or staff_list; give this or the email, not both

tools.name: users_enable
tools.description: Prepare enabling a disabled person in Answerable ID, so that they can sign in again where their membership is in force. Name them by email or userId. A person who is Answerable staff needs the owner role. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. Sessions, grants and tokens revoked when they were disabled stay revoked, and a person whose address was retired cannot be enabled.

email.description: Their address as Answerable ID holds it, in any case; give this or the id, not both

userId.description: Their user id, from members_list or staff_list; give this or the email, not both

tools.name: users_retireemail
tools.description: Prepare retiring the address of a disabled person in Answerable ID, for good, so that another person can hold it. Name them by email or userId; users_disable them first. Owner only, with a recent sign-in at your directory. Changes nothing: returns a preview; show the person its summary, then commit the intent with admin_commit_confirmed and that summary. It cannot be undone: the next holder of the address is a new person with a new sub.

email.description: Their address as Answerable ID holds it, in any case; give this or the id, not both

userId.description: Their user id, from members_list or staff_list; give this or the email, not both
